sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3. This is the Second Bail Cancellation Application.
The First Bail Cancellation was dismissed in non-prosecution on 03.01.2023.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that, in fact, the private respondent had filed a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in which a statement was given by the private respondents that they would settle the dispute with the applicant, who is the informant of the case, and obtained interim order.
But the private respondents did not settle the dispute.
Therefore, the interim order was subsequently vacated.
But, these facts were not brought to the notice of the Court while considering the bail application.
In addition to it, it is also argued that the trial has yet not been concluded and the private respondents are extending threats.

5. Insofar as non disclosure of the proceedings under Section 482 of the Code is concerned, perhaps,
it has no effect on the bail order because ultimately what had happened is that the interim order was Ramesh Kumar vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76534541/
1 vacated and pursuant thereto, the private respondents appeared and sought bail.

entities.text: Ramesh Kumar vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. As far as delay in trial is concerned, there may be various reasons for delay in the trial.
Is it because of the private respondents?
If it is so, the informant is always free to bring it to the notice of the court concerned, inviting court's attention on the conduct of the private respondents.
Merely on the basis of a statement that the private respondents are extending threats, this Court cannot quash the bail order granted by the court below.
Perhaps, this may be brought to the notice of the court concerned as subsequent conduct of a person, post grant of bail.
7. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court is of the view that there is no reason to consider cancellation of bail.
The bail cancellation application deserves to be dismissed.
8. The bail cancellation application is dismissed.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 23.03.2023
